verdict.rationale: Obsidian Sync docs claim you can 'collaborate on a shared vault with your team' and offers version history for conflicts, but hands-on community evidence indicates native sync isn't built for real-time concurrent editing — one user built a separate CRDT-based collaboration plugin (Relay) specifically because Sync/Git-based approaches aren't good for 'device sync or collaboration' without stepping on changes. Missing for 10: first-party evidence of real-time conflict-free co-editing (e.g., operational transform/CRDT merging), independent confirmation that simultaneous edits don't create conflicts, and clarity on how version history resolves concurrent edits.
